# Remove Series Names in Bulk

> Operator, 2026-08-06: *"In previous matching, my series and episode titles got all messed up. I'd like to be able to select groups of series titles to delete them in batch. Some are good and should stay — some come from the source and some come from me, used to organize the collection (e.g. I set the series name for all ‹series› videos, 122 of them, so the episode numbers sorting view would work)."*
## Why this is possible at all
⚠️ **Series is the one entity that is not a node.** `Asset.videoName` is a free-text column by a decision the Library Graph Epic took deliberately, since roughly 5% of the library carries one. So a series name has **no profile, no provenance and no confirmed state** — nothing records who wrote it.
That is precisely why the damage happened: a match writes into the same column the operator uses to organise a collection by hand. Two very different things share one field, and the field cannot tell them apart.
## What the tool can and cannot know
It can measure two things, and they separate the cases well in practice:
| Signal | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **How many videos share the name** | A series exists to group videos. One grouping 122 is an organising decision; one grouping a single video is usually a title that arrived with a match. |
| **How many of those were matched to a source** | ⚠️ A **hint**, never provenance — a video the operator named and later matched counts here too. It says "worth looking at", not "this came from the source". |
Both are shown per row. Neither is presented as a verdict.
## The screen
**Series Gallery → Clean Up → Remove Names…** The gallery's single button became a menu, because there are now two opposite things you can do to a series name: **Standardize** keeps a name and tidies its variants, **Remove** takes it off entirely.
Destructive and not undoable inside the app, so it is built to make keeping easy and removing deliberate:
- **Nothing is pre-selected.**
- **Most-used names lead**, so the entries most likely worth keeping are visible without scrolling.
- **The affected video count is on the button** — *Remove 47* — rather than discovered afterwards.
- A **"Select the N used by one video"** shortcut for the common case, labelled explicitly as a shortcut rather than a verdict.
- Search, because a library with hundreds of stray names is exactly the one this is for.
## 🚨 The decision that matters
**Clearing a series name does NOT clear episode numbering by default.**
The operator's own case is the reason: they set a series name *so that* the episode numbers would sort. The numbering is theirs and is the more valuable half of the record. Removing it as a side effect of removing a name would destroy exactly what the name existed to serve.
An explicit toggle — *"Also clear season, episode number and episode title"* — covers the opposite case, where a bad match wrote the whole block and all of it is wrong. Off every time the screen opens.
Nothing else on the record is touched; pinned by a test asserting tags, rating, notes and id all survive.
